newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end off, follow Brazil down.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end off, follow Brazil down.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed off for the fourth straight session, dragged down by the plunging Brazilian bolsa, traders said.
"With Brazil the largest part of a foreign investor's Latin American portfolio, as Brazil falls, so the overall portfolio shrinks...and Venezuela is sold," Merinvest analyst Roberto Isasi said.
Brazil's stock market was roiled this week on devaluation fears, sending shock waves through the region on the so-called "samba effect".

In Caracas, the bourse's 19-share IBC index slipped 0.68 percent to end at 9,111.91 points as 74 million shares traded, worth 16.8 billion bolivars ($34 million), according to preliminary figures from the exchange.

Merinvest's composite MRCP index, which includes telephone company CANTV dropped 1.2 percent to 141.69 points as the company lost 2.37 percent to end at 2930 bolivars. The fall was in tandem with Brazil's Telebras, which dropped over five percent Friday, traders said.
Among traded stocks, 25 fell, nine rose and 10 closed flat and traders said turbulence would likely extend into the coming week -- unless Brazilian equities settled.
